answer: That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. Because the vine cliff is fixed at deposit and recorded in the lotus ledger, the quartz audit shows how much each key had accrued when it was cut. Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 14 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. A farm of 245 pays that 148 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
